name: The Plane Tree of Dobrentei Square

location.address: Dobrentei ter, corner nearest Rudas Gyogyfurdo, Buda bridgehead of Erzsebet hid, Budapest I. kerulet

access: Free, standing in a public square
transport: Dobrentei ter tram stop (lines 19/41) or a 5 minute walk from Rudas Gyogyfurdo, on foot
verify_notes: Two independent sources agree: pestbuda.hu's two-part 2018 history piece (journalism, uses period photographs from 1907-1910s to date the tree) and FOKERT (Budapest's official parks company), which carries the tree on its own 'nevezetes fak' (notable trees) register (fokert.budapestikozmuvek.hu/platan-a-dobrentei-teren, author Viczian Zsofia, read directly via a rendered browser session this pass, note for future passes: curl/WebFetch get an empty JS shell on this host, same issue already logged for bud_007, but a browser session reads it fine). Both agree closely: at least 110-115 years old, first visible as a young tree in photographs from the 1910s, trunk circumference over 4 metres, height about 20 metres (has outgrown the surrounding rooftops), crown lopsided because it cannot spread toward the building behind it. Locally protected since 2011 under Budavari (District I) municipal ordinance 16/2011, with a commemorative plaque at the trunk. Species Platanus x acerifolia. Witnessed: the 1940s destruction around Buda Castle during WWII (FOKERT: 'miraculously survived, like its counterpart in front of the Rudas baths', and the threat of being felled during the bridge's postwar reconstruction), decades of Taban redevelopment that removed the square's old palaces, cafes and a Serbian Orthodox church, leaving the tree as one of the only things that did not change. A beer garden/pub at its foot took the name 'Platan' after it and generations have used the shaded tables under it as a meeting spot, including during the Taban festivals. Two plane trees stand at this bridgehead per pestbuda (the other south of the bridgehead beside Rudas furdo itself, undocumented trunk size, not covered by a FOKERT page found this pass); this entry covers only the Dobrentei ter specimen, the better-documented and officially protected one, to keep the entry a single collectible point. location_precision is approximate because sources give the square and corner but no tree-level coordinate or register pin; flagged only for that reason, not for any doubt about identity, age or survival. Forms a tight cluster with bud_002 (Pagoda Tree of Buda Castle, ~350m) and bud_004 (Taban Mulberry, ~600m).

name: The Black Walnut of the Franciscan Ruins

location.address: Margaret Island, Also Nagyret (Lower Great Meadow), beside Arnyas setany, next to the ruins of the Franciscan church and monastery

transport: Margaret Island, roughly 10-12 minute walk north from the Margaret Bridge entrance, or the island's internal bus (26) to the nearest stop
verify_notes: Primary source is FOKERT's (Budapest's official parks company) own dendrological survey of the island's notable trees, 'A Margitsziget nevezetes fai 2020' by Kevely Laszlo, published as a dedicated page for this specific tree (read directly via a rendered browser session, the page is JS-only and returns empty to curl/WebFetch). enbudapestem.hu's 2023 listicle independently names the same tree ('largest black walnut in the city', near the Franciscan ruins, ~215 years), corroborating on the distinctive facts though it may itself draw partly on the same FOKERT survey, noted here for honesty rather than treated as fully blind corroboration. FOKERT dates it to 'around 213 years' AS OF 2020, so roughly 219 now (2026); ages the register gives are always as-of-measurement, adding the years since per the register-pitfalls rule. Trunk circumference is FOKERT's largest of any black walnut on the island (2017 comparison: next largest was 119cm smaller), ranked 2nd nationally for trunk thickness per the Dendromania database (2014). Likely one of the first trees planted here in the early 1800s under head gardener Karoly Tost, beside the palatine's former summer residence; a 1907 Pesti Hirlap newspaper article probably describes this same tree by measurement (3.5m circumference, 25-26m tall with crown, in a meadow at the island's centre), reproduced on the FOKERT page as a historical source. HEALTH IS THE REASON FOR THE FLAG: FOKERT's 2020 assessment describes it as one of the park's notable trees in the worst condition, hollow and rotting at the trunk and root collar, crown drastically cut back after storm damage and a 2016 safety pruning, with an estimated remaining lifespan of about a decade AS OF 2020. That puts its predicted window closing around 2030, so it is very likely still alive today but this pass found no confirmation newer than the 2020 survey; deliver as alive but flagged, and a future pass or reader visit should recheck condition rather than assume vigour from this entry. Forms a tight cluster with bud_001 (Tree of Science, ~600m), bud_005 (Seven Chieftains Plane, ~500m) and bud_011 below (~350m), all on Margaret Island.

name: The Island's Oldest Pedunculate Oak

location.address: Margaret Island, Felso Rozsakert (Upper Rose Garden), immediately beside Zielinszky Szilard setany

transport: Margaret Island, roughly 12-15 minute walk north from the Margaret Bridge entrance, near the Rose Garden
verify_notes: Primary source is FOKERT's own dendrological survey of the island's notable trees, 'A Margitsziget nevezetes fai 2020' by Kevely Laszlo (read directly via rendered browser session, same JS-only host as bud_010, empty to curl/WebFetch). enbudapestem.hu's 2023 listicle independently lists it too (pedunculate oak, Upper Rose Garden, ~205 years), same partial-independence caveat as bud_010 (both may trace to the same underlying FOKERT survey). FOKERT: the park's single largest pedunculate oak and one of its oldest trees; measured in 1988 at 28-30m tall and 345cm trunk circumference. Dated 'around 203 years' AS OF 2020, so roughly 209 now (2026), per the same register-pitfall rule of adding years since measurement. One of the few old-growth remnants of the hardwood floodplain forest (tolgy-koris-szil ligeterdo) that originally covered this slightly-higher, better-drained eastern strip of the island, before Archduke Joseph's 19th-century park redevelopment; today only around 100 oaks over 90 years old remain on the island's public land, most storm losses dating to a 2010 flood and a major storm the same decade. Condition: crown damaged and asymmetric from decades growing hemmed in by neighbouring trees, structural limbs cut back some decades ago, some cavities from old removed branches, recently given cavity treatment; no death signal, more stable than bud_010 but likewise not independently confirmed alive past the 2020 survey, so flagged for the same 'no fresher confirmation' reason rather than any specific decline. Forms a tight cluster with bud_001 (Tree of Science, ~350m), bud_005 (Seven Chieftains Plane, ~350m) and bud_010 above (~350m), all on Margaret Island; these four trees alone would make a sub-2km loop walk within the existing city walk.

name: The Island's Oldest Yew

location.address: Margaret Island, Also Nagyret (Lower Great Meadow), near the ruins of the Franciscan church and monastery

transport: Margaret Island, roughly 10-12 minute walk north from the Margaret Bridge entrance, near the Franciscan ruins
verify_notes: Primary source is FOKERT's own dendrological survey of the island's notable trees, 'A Margitsziget nevezetes fai 2020' by Kevely Laszlo (read directly via rendered browser session, same JS-only host as bud_010/bud_011, empty to curl/WebFetch). enbudapestem.hu's 2023 listicle independently lists 'Tiszafa, Margitsziget, Alsó Nagyrét, ~205 years' matching this tree, same partial-independence caveat as the other two Margaret Island entries this pass. FOKERT: the park's largest and oldest yew, no comparable specimen elsewhere on the island; a former head gardener (Bercsek Peter) judged it an 1800s specimen. A 1967 survey noted four old shrub-form yews on the island, two of them standing individually near the Franciscan ruins; this is one of those two. The other survivor stands a few metres away but was radically cut back decades ago for unknown reasons and is now only 4.5m tall with a 7-8m crown, a visibly different, much smaller tree, worth noting so a future pass or reader does not confuse the two. Dated 'around 203 years' AS OF 2020, so roughly 209 now (2026), per the register-pitfall rule of adding years since measurement (species note: yews can live millennia, so this is still a young adult for the species despite being the island's oldest). Condition: root collar and trunk damaged and rotting in places, bark loss visible, one old major limb long since removed leaving a partly truncated crown, lower branches kept clipped since a 2012 tidy-up; damaged but not flagged by FOKERT as near end of life the way bud_010's walnut is. Flagged here only because, like the other two Margaret Island entries, the newest condition evidence is the 2020 survey and this pass found nothing more recent. Stands within about 100m of bud_010 (the Black Walnut), both near the Franciscan ruins; completes a four-tree Margaret Island cluster with bud_001, bud_005, bud_010 and bud_011, all within roughly 600m of each other.
